title: Implement API Rate Limiting
question: Design and implement rate limiting for a REST API. Requirements: 1) Limit requests per user/IP, 2) Different rate limits for different endpoints, 3) Graceful degradation with proper error messages, 4) Distributed rate limiting across multiple instances, 5) Rate limit headers in responses, 6) Admin endpoints bypass rate limits. Discuss: using Bucket4j library with Spring Boot, implementing token bucket algorithm for smooth rate limiting, storing rate limit state in Redis for distributed tracking, using @RateLimit custom annotation on controller methods, implementing servlet filter or interceptor for rate limit checks, extracting user ID or IP address for rate limit key, configuring different limits per endpoint (100/min for reads, 10/min for writes), returning 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header, adding X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset headers to all responses, implementing sliding window for more accurate rate limiting, using @ConditionalOnExpression to bypass rate limiting for admin roles, monitoring rate limit violations with metrics, implementing rate limit warming (gradual increase), and testing rate limiting under load.

title: Comprehensive API Versioning
question: Implement a comprehensive API versioning strategy. Requirements: 1) Support multiple active versions simultaneously, 2) Version discovery mechanism, 3) Deprecation strategy with sunset dates, 4) Backward compatibility, 5) Version-specific documentation, 6) Gradual migration support. Discuss: choosing versioning approach (URI path /v1/users, request header Accept: application/vnd.api.v1+json, or query param ?version=1), implementing URI versioning with @RequestMapping("/api/v1"), using content negotiation for header-based versioning, creating separate controller classes per version for maintainability, sharing common DTOs and services across versions using adapters, implementing version-specific converters to transform between versions, using @Deprecated annotation and deprecation headers (Sunset, Deprecation), creating separate OpenAPI documentation per version using GroupedOpenAPI, implementing version routing filter to direct requests to correct version, using feature flags to enable/disable specific versions, monitoring usage by version to plan deprecation, implementing automatic migration suggestions in responses, providing version changelog in documentation, and testing cross-version compatibility.

title: Advanced Pagination, Filtering, and Sorting
question: Implement comprehensive pagination, filtering, and sorting for list APIs. Requirements: 1) Cursor-based and offset-based pagination, 2) Dynamic filtering on multiple fields, 3) Multi-column sorting, 4) Performance optimization for large datasets, 5) Consistent query syntax, 6) Metadata in responses. Discuss: implementing Pageable support with @PageableDefault for offset pagination, creating custom Page wrapper with links to next/prev/first/last pages, implementing cursor-based pagination using keyset pagination for better performance, encoding cursor as base64 (id + timestamp) to prevent manipulation, implementing @FilterParam custom annotation for type-safe filtering, using Specification pattern (Spring Data JPA) for dynamic query building, parsing filter syntax like ?filter=status:eq:active,age:gt:18, implementing sort with multiple columns ?sort=name:asc,createdAt:desc, optimizing database queries with proper indexes, including total count conditionally (expensive for large datasets), adding pagination metadata (page, size, totalElements, totalPages, hasNext, hasPrevious), implementing HATEOAS links for discoverability, validating page size limits to prevent performance issues, caching filtered/sorted results when appropriate, and testing with millions of records.

title: Design Bulk Operations API
question: Design REST API for bulk operations (create, update, delete multiple resources). Requirements: 1) Accept array of items in single request, 2) Partial success handling, 3) Transaction management options, 4) Progress tracking, 5) Performance optimization, 6) Error reporting per item. Discuss: designing endpoint POST /api/v1/users/bulk accepting array of user objects, implementing batch processing with configurable chunk size, using @Transactional with appropriate propagation (REQUIRED for all-or-nothing, REQUIRES_NEW per item), implementing partial success with 207 Multi-Status response containing per-item results, creating detailed response with success/failure array indicating which items succeeded, using CompletableFuture for parallel processing of independent items, implementing async processing with 202 Accepted for very large batches, returning operation ID for status tracking via GET /api/v1/operations/{id}, using database batch insert/update (JDBC batch) for performance, implementing idempotency keys to prevent duplicate processing on retries, adding validation per item with clear error messages, limiting bulk size (max 1000 items) with proper error, monitoring bulk operation performance and failure rates, implementing bulk delete with soft delete for safety, and testing with concurrent bulk operations.

title: Long-Running Operations API
question: Design REST API for long-running asynchronous operations. Requirements: 1) Immediate response with operation ID, 2) Status polling endpoint, 3) Optional webhooks for completion, 4) Cancellation support, 5) Result retrieval, 6) TTL for operation results. Discuss: implementing POST endpoint returning 202 Accepted with Location header pointing to status URL, generating unique operation ID (UUID) stored in database/Redis, returning response {operationId, status: 'PENDING', statusUrl: '/api/operations/{id}'}, implementing @Async service method for background processing, creating GET /api/operations/{id} endpoint returning {status: 'PROCESSING'|'COMPLETED'|'FAILED', progress: 75, result, error}, using DeferredResult or CompletableFuture for async controller methods, implementing DELETE /api/operations/{id} for cancellation using interrupt or flag, storing results in Redis with TTL (24 hours) for retrieval, implementing webhook notification on completion if callback URL provided, using SSE (Server-Sent Events) for real-time progress updates as alternative to polling, adding Retry-After header to suggest polling interval, implementing operation expiry and cleanup job, monitoring operation duration and success rates, handling operation failures with retry mechanism, and testing timeout scenarios.

title: Robust File Upload API
question: Design a robust file upload API with validation and security. Requirements: 1) Single and multiple file uploads, 2) File type validation, 3) Size limits, 4) Virus scanning, 5) Progress tracking, 6) Resumable uploads for large files, 7) Direct cloud storage upload. Discuss: implementing POST /api/files with @RequestParam MultipartFile for file upload, configuring spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size and max-request-size, validating file types using MIME type checking and magic number verification (not just extension), implementing custom @ValidFile annotation with ConstraintValidator, integrating ClamAV or similar for virus scanning before processing, returning file metadata {fileId, filename, size, uploadedAt}, implementing chunked upload with POST /api/files/{id}/chunks for resumable uploads, storing chunk metadata in Redis, using @Async for large file processing, generating presigned URLs for direct-to-S3 upload to avoid server bandwidth, implementing upload progress using WebSocket or SSE, storing files in object storage (S3, GCS) instead of local filesystem, generating thumbnail/preview for images asynchronously, implementing file access control with permissions, adding file expiry and automatic deletion, monitoring upload failures and file storage costs, implementing deduplication using content hash, and testing with large files (GB+).

title: Full-Text Search API
question: Design a full-text search API with advanced features. Requirements: 1) Multi-field search, 2) Fuzzy matching and typo tolerance, 3) Faceted search/filtering, 4) Relevance scoring, 5) Autocomplete suggestions, 6) Search analytics. Discuss: integrating Elasticsearch or Solr for full-text search capabilities, implementing GET /api/search?q=query&filters=category:books&sort=relevance, using @Query with full-text indexes in database for simple cases, implementing fuzzy matching with Levenshtein distance for typo tolerance, creating inverted indexes on searchable fields, implementing autocomplete with GET /api/search/suggestions?q=partial using prefix matching or n-grams, adding faceted search returning count by category/price range/etc, boosting relevance of certain fields (title boost 3x, description 1x), implementing search filters with AND/OR/NOT operators, highlighting matching terms in results, implementing search-as-you-type with debouncing, caching popular search queries in Redis, logging search queries for analytics (popular terms, zero-result searches), implementing pagination with cursor for consistent results, adding spelling correction suggestions, monitoring search performance and relevance, implementing synonym handling, and testing search quality with relevance metrics.

title: Webhook Delivery System
question: Design a webhook delivery system for event notifications. Requirements: 1) Event subscription management, 2) Reliable delivery with retries, 3) Signature verification, 4) Delivery status tracking, 5) Webhook testing, 6) Rate limiting per subscriber. Discuss: implementing webhook registration endpoint POST /api/webhooks with {url, events: ['order.created'], secret}, storing webhook configurations in database, implementing event publishing using ApplicationEventPublisher when business events occur, using @Async for non-blocking webhook delivery, implementing retry with exponential backoff (retry after 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 5 attempts), generating HMAC signature using shared secret for payload verification, adding signature in X-Webhook-Signature header, implementing webhook deactivation after consecutive failures, creating GET /api/webhooks/{id}/deliveries for delivery history, implementing webhook testing endpoint POST /api/webhooks/{id}/test, implementing per-subscriber rate limiting to prevent abuse, using message queue (RabbitMQ/Kafka) for reliable webhook queue, adding webhook payload versioning, implementing webhook timeout (5 seconds), logging delivery attempts with status codes, monitoring webhook success rates per subscriber, implementing webhook rotation for security, and testing webhook failures and retries.
